# Native Context fixtures for Harness generation capture

`native-context.json` is generated by the tracked native Rust example
`context-manager/examples/generation_capture_fixtures.rs`, not by Harness tests.
It contains one complete `context::assemble` input/output pair and seven
`render_system_prompt_with_span` outputs. Both are real production APIs.
The example reuses the in-memory ports in `context-manager/tests/common/fakes.rs`
(the assembly reference is `tests/origin_binding.rs`); the summarizer returns
fixed public synthetic text. No engine, provider, model, or private data is used.

From the repository root, regenerate and then verify without modifying the oracle:

```sh
CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true SKIP_UI_BUILD=1 SKIP_CONSOLE_UI_BUILD=1 \
  cargo run --manifest-path context-manager/Cargo.toml --locked --offline \
  --example generation_capture_fixtures
CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true SKIP_UI_BUILD=1 SKIP_CONSOLE_UI_BUILD=1 \
  cargo run --manifest-path context-manager/Cargo.toml --locked --offline \
  --example generation_capture_fixtures -- --check
```

`--check` generates into a fresh `TempDir` and compares exact JSON bytes with
this fixture; drift fails. `--output DIR` regenerates elsewhere for review.
The generator prints the byte count and SHA-256. Review producer changes before
accepting regenerated data. The assembly's random correlation `assembly_id` is
the **only** normalized output field; all prompt bytes, SHA-256 hashes, byte spans,
indices, budgets, messages, and other output fields are produced by Context.

Memory cases retain the ordered/reordered/noncontiguous/base-copy scenarios of
the former local renderer source, now reproduced by the tracked example.
Summary negative cases also use actual renderer-produced hashes/spans; only
intentional authority and wrong-span mutations remain in the consumer tests.
Harness includes the tracked bytes at compile time and uses a fresh `TempDir`
for each test's diagnostic writes. Ordinary tests never run this generator,
read ignored inputs, or depend on another test's output or execution order.
